demonstrations.title: Possibility is not capability
demonstrations.summary: An editorial decision showing why a possible event should not be rewritten as an event someone has the ability or authority to cancel.

concept.subject: Preserving modality during direct revision
concept.textAlternative: Text summary: Original: The event may be canceled if severe weather continues. Possible revision: The event can be canceled if severe weather continues. Decision: do not apply the revision; preserve may because possibility is not capability.

fields.value: The event may be canceled if severe weather continues.
The event can be canceled if severe weather continues.
Do not apply this revision. Preserve may.
May describes an uncertain outcome here. Can may describe ability, authority, or permission, so the proposed substitution would change the claim.
Possibility, the severe-weather condition, and the event remain intact.
No wording changes in this example.
The sentence remains unchanged because the proposed edit would convert possibility into capability.

limitations: This illustration explains one editorial distinction and does not execute PasteLint.
The decision is bounded to the sentence and context shown.
demonstrations.notes: DEMO-002 remains reserved for the documented future Clean live-engine candidate. This concept illustration replaces an existing article comparison without claiming live execution.

demonstrations.title: Preparation stops before acceptance
demonstrations.summary: A destination-readiness progression that keeps preparation distinct from publication and downstream acceptance.

concept.subject: The evidence boundary between preparation and downstream acceptance
concept.textAlternative: Text summary: Draft, reviewed, prepared, then ready for destination. PasteLint can report preparation; publication or downstream acceptance requires evidence from the destination.

fields.value: Evidence boundary: Preparation does not establish publication or downstream acceptance.
PasteLint can observe the preparation it performs. Publication, deployment, delivery, and acceptance require evidence from the receiving system.

limitations: This is a conceptual workflow illustration and does not observe a downstream destination.
Ready for destination does not mean published, deployed, delivered, or accepted.
demonstrations.notes: This illustration reuses the article's existing handoff argument and introduces no product state or downstream claim.
